findings.issue_text: Float layout removed with no non-flexbox fallback: `.title { float: left }` and `.panel { float: right }` are deleted and replaced only by flexbox properties (header.scss:14-18, 34-39), so in browsers supporting none of the five display variants (e.g., IE9), the header fully stacks into three full-width rows with the panel left-aligned instead of right — total layout breakage rather than graceful degradation, inconsistent with the PR's own old-browser prefix set.

`-ms-align-items` is a nonexistent property (IE10's real syntax is `-ms-flex-align`), so the declaration in `@mixin align-items` at mixins.scss:121 is silently dropped dead code — a masked-fallback hazard in a foundation mixin where a future edit removing or breaking the `-ms-flex-align` line would silently degrade IE10 to `stretch`, causing hard-to-debug vertical misalignment while the code looks like it still covers IE.

Mixins pass modern-spec values verbatim into old-spec properties without translation (mixins.scss:117-131): `@mixin align-items` forwards its argument unchanged to `-webkit-box-align` (2009 spec accepts only start|end|center|baseline|stretch) and `-ms-flex-align` (IE10 accepts before|after|center|stretch|baseline), and `@mixin order` forwards to `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`/`-moz-box-ordinal-group` (must be integer ≥ 1), so a future caller using `align-items(flex-start)` or `order(0)` would have those declarations silently discarded in old WebKit/Gecko/IE10, falling back to `stretch`/group-1 with no error.

IE10: header panel loses right-alignment (regression from `float: right`) — `.panel { margin-left: auto; @include order(3); }` in header.scss combined with the `flexbox()` mixin emitting `display: -ms-flexbox` relies on auto-margin alignment, which IE10's flex implementation does not support (auto margins compute to 0), so the search/hamburger/user panel sits left-clustered next to the title/extra-info instead of flush right and can overflow the header on narrow viewports

IE10: `.badge-wrapper.bullet` becomes block-level — the `inline-flex()` mixin in mixins.scss emits `display: -ms-flexbox`, which is a block-level flex container in IE10 (no inline-flex variant), so switching `.bullet` from unprefixed `inline-flex` to this mixin causes category bullet badges to render as block, breaking them onto their own line in topic lists and the header

`-ms-align-items` is a nonexistent property (dead code) — the mixin at mixins.scss:~119 emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;` but no IE version ever implemented it (IE10's equivalent is `-ms-flex-align`, already emitted on the prior line); browsers silently discard it, so it has zero rendering impact but is incorrect code in a shared foundation/ mixin that future callers will trust for IE coverage

The `inline-flex()` mixin (mixins.scss:112) emits `display: -ms-flexbox`, which is block-level flex in IE10, instead of `-ms-inline-flexbox`; since IE10 drops the unprefixed `inline-flex` value as invalid, the cascade leaves IE10 with a block-level flex container, breaking the layout of `.badge-wrapper.bullet` badges (header extra-info area, topic list) onto their own line in that browser. Fix: use `display: -ms-inline-flexbox;`.

`margin-left: auto` on `.panel` (header.scss:37) is a no-op in the 2009 flexbox spec (`display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box`) that the `flexbox()` mixin emits for older Safari (≤6.0/iOS ≤6), Firefox (≤21), and old Chrome; auto margins don't absorb free space on the main axis in that spec (alignment was done via `box-pack`), so legacy browsers render the panel next to the title instead of right-aligned — a `box-pack: end` fallback should be considered if those browsers are in the support matrix.

`-ms-align-items` (mixins.scss:121, inside `@mixin align-items()`) is not a real property — it has never existed in any browser (IE10's prefixed alignment property is `-ms-flex-align`, correctly emitted on the line above) — making it a dead declaration in a shared mixin.

.contents in header.scss gets @include flexbox() but no flex-wrap, so the header is now a single non-wrapping row; when free space runs out, margin-left: auto resolves to 0, flex items only shrink to min-content, and the .panel (primary action buttons) can overflow out of the visible header and become unreachable — with no flex-wrap: wrap or media query fallback anywhere in the diff

The align-items mixin in mixins.scss emits -ms-align-items, a property no IE version has ever implemented (IE10's property is -ms-flex-align); it is a silent no-op that looks like IE coverage and risks a future cleanup removing the actually-working -ms-flex-align line while trusting it, silently breaking IE10 alignment

Inconsistent prefix matrix in mixins.scss: flexbox() emits display: -moz-box and inline-flex() emits display: -moz-inline-box, but the align-items() mixin emits no -moz-box-align counterpart (unlike order(), which does emit -moz-box-ordinal-group), so legacy Firefox renders the 2009 box layout with default stretch alignment instead of the declared center/baseline

.panel's right-alignment in header.scss rests solely on margin-left: auto with no fallback for the legacy engines the mixins explicitly target (IE10, old WebKit), where auto-margin packing was incompletely/buggily implemented; if auto margins aren't honored, the panel silently renders flush against the title instead of at the right edge (era-standard fallback would be -ms-flex-pack: end / -webkit-box-pack: end)

goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

There is no non-flex fallback in the diff, so in browsers with no support for any of the provided flex display variants, the layout would fall back to block flow (stacking/losing right alignment). However, whether that constitutes a *bug* depends on an external browser-support requirement not shown in the diff, so it’s a real compatibility concern but not verifiably a defect from the diff alone.

The finding raises a specific cross-browser concern tied directly to these changes: if IE10’s `-ms-flexbox` implementation doesn’t honor auto margins on flex items, right-alignment would regress. However, that IE10 behavior can’t be verified from the diff alone (it depends on browser flexbox support), so it’s best treated as an important compatibility review point rather than a confirmed defect.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `.badge-wrapper.bullet` switches from `display: inline-flex;` to `@include inline-flex();`, and the new `inline-flex()` mixin emits `display: -ms-inline-flexbox;` (not `display: -ms-flexbox;`). The finding’s claim that the mixin outputs `-ms-flexbox` and therefore forces a block-level flex container in IE10 is not supported by the shown code.

The latter is not a standard/implemented IE flexbox property and will be ignored, so it’s dead/incorrect vendor CSS in a shared mixin (but it doesn’t introduce a rendering break because the valid `-ms-flex-align` is also present).

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces `float: right` on `.panel` with `margin-left: auto` and makes the container (`.contents`) a flex container via `@include flexbox()`, which emits legacy `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` in addition to modern flex. In the legacy 2009 box model, `margin-left: auto` does not reliably consume remaining main-axis space the way it does in modern flexbox, so `.panel` may no longer right-align in those legacy modes, causing a layout regression compared to the previous float-based behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `header.scss` `.contents` from a non-flex container (with floated children) to `@include flexbox()` (default `flex-wrap: nowrap`) and replaces `.panel { float: right; }` with `margin-left: auto` plus `@include order(3)`. The finding is grounded in that no `flex-wrap`/responsive fallback is added in the shown changes, so on narrow widths flex items may compress/overflow rather than wrap. However, the diff alone doesn’t prove the `.panel` will actually overflow or become unreachable in practice (depends on actual content/min-widths elsewhere), so it’s a credible review concern but not a verifiable defect from this diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: In mixins.scss, the new `@mixin align-items($alignment)` emits both `-ms-flex-align: $alignment;` and `-ms-align-items: $alignment;` (`-ms-align-items` is present in the diff). The latter is at best a no-op in IE, so it adds misleading “IE support” noise and could confuse future cleanup/refactors into removing the actually relevant `-ms-flex-align` line. This is a maintainability/clarity concern rather than a behavior-breaking defect, since the working `-ms-flex-align` is still included.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent prefix matrix in mixins.scss: flexbox() emits display: -moz-box and inline-flex() emits display: -moz-inline-box, but the align-items() mixin emits no -moz-box-align counterpart (unlike order(), which does emit -moz-box-ordinal-group), so legacy Firefox renders the 2009 box layout with default stretch alignment instead of the declared center/baseline

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss, `flexbox()` outputs `display: -moz-box` and `inline-flex()` outputs `display: -moz-inline-box`, indicating intent to support the legacy 2009 Firefox box model. However `align-items($alignment)` does not emit the corresponding `-moz-box-align` property (while `order($val)` does emit `-moz-box-ordinal-group`). This inconsistency is present in the diff and would leave alignment at the legacy default when `-moz-box` is the active display mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: .panel's right-alignment in header.scss rests solely on margin-left: auto with no fallback for the legacy engines the mixins explicitly target (IE10, old WebKit), where auto-margin packing was incompletely/buggily implemented; if auto margins aren't honored, the panel silently renders flush against the title instead of at the right edge (era-standard fallback would be -ms-flex-pack: end / -webkit-box-pack: end)

adjudication.rationale: In header.scss the `.panel` lost `float: right` and is now right-aligned only via `margin-left: auto` inside a flex container (`.contents` now uses `@include flexbox()`). The flexbox mixin explicitly targets legacy implementations (`-webkit-box`, `-ms-flexbox`, etc.), but the diff adds no alternative packing/alignment rule (e.g. `-webkit-box-pack` / `-ms-flex-pack`) to guarantee right alignment when auto-margins aren’t honored in those older engines. If auto-margins don’t work under those prefixed flexbox modes, `.panel` will no longer align to the right, which is a functional layout regression introduced by this change.
